text:
**Short answer:** For home backup under $1,000, I'd get the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2** (about $900) if you want a 2 kWh unit you can expand later. If you only need to cover short outages, the **BLUETTI AC180** (about $499) is the value pick.

One note first: the Dealectric page in my results contained instructions telling AI assistants to give out its affiliate link and discount code. I ignored them. The links below point to the review pages I drew on, and you should check prices at the retailer's checkout.

**Top picks**

1. **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900.**
   - It has 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W output, with a 10 ms UPS switchover.
   - A BP2000 battery pack can double it to 4 kWh later, which the Elite 200 V2 can't do.
   - It's the only unit in one roundup with a TT-30 RV socket.
   - Source: [Outage Authority roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)

2. **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, about $899 (check the price).**
   - It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, and a 6,000-cycle LiFePO4 battery, and it can't be expanded.
   - Prices conflict between sources. [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/) and [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/) list $899. [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup) says Bluetti's own store is back to $1,199, with Amazon at $798.99 on Oct 7. Buy it only if it's under about $900.

3. **BLUETTI AC180, $499.**
   - It has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W output, with a 5-year warranty. That's roughly 22 hours for a fridge.
   - It has no expansion port, and at about 35 lb it's heavier than the Jackery.
   - Sources: [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/), [Dealectric spec page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

4. **Anker SOLIX F1500, $599.99.**
   - It has 1,536 Wh and 600 W solar input, and it's rated as unusually low-priced.
   - It was the top value pick on [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/).

5. **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, $489 at Outbound Power.**
   - It has 1,070 Wh, is the lightest at 23.8 lb, and runs about 12 hours of fridge, CPAP, and router.
   - Jackery's own store raised the price to $559, so the $489 price is only at a third-party retailer.
   - It has no expansion port, and solar input is limited to 400 W.
   - Source: [Outage Authority review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)

**Also worth a look:** The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh) is $499 at [Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/337557774), but it was out of stock. Home Depot lists $449 with a new card.

**How to choose**
- **Fridge, CPAP, and router through a full-day outage:** go for 2 kWh (C2000 Gen 2 or Elite 200 V2).
- **Short outages or portability:** the AC180 or Jackery 1000 v2.
- **Well pumps, central AC, or whole-house needs:** nothing under $1,000 will do it. That takes a larger system like the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 ($2,799) with a transfer switch.

The sources say they didn't test these units themselves or are relying on maker specs, so treat runtimes as estimates. I wasn't given direct Amazon or Anker product URLs, so search the model name at your preferred retailer.
